channel.title: The Smithfield Times - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Smithfield Times (smithfieldtimes.com)

item.title: IW School Board calls special meeting after SHS anti-ICE protest
item.description: Isle of Wight County's School Board has called a special closed meeting tonight partially in response to Smithfield High’s student-led anti-ICE walkout last week.

item.title: Suspect in Woods Edge shooting arrested after year-long, multi-agency search
item.description: After just over a year on the run, Anthony Lamont Haywood was arrested in Portsmouth on 12 felony charges tied to a 2025 Woods Edge shooting in Smithfield.

item.title: No action taken against IWCS staff at School Board meeting after ICE protest
item.description: After a student-led anti-ICE walkout at Smithfield High, Isle of Wight’s School Board held a special meeting but took no action against any school employees who allowed the protest.

item.title: Town Council votes 6-1 to purchase Grange site for $6.5M
item.description: Smithfield's Town Council voted 6-1 on March 3 to buy the 57-acre former Grange at 10Main site for $6.5 million from developer Joseph Luter IV.

item.title: Letter – Selective support for Bill of Rights
item.description: Letter: Smithfield resident Rosie Simmons calls John Edwards' column from last week a “selective” defense of the Bill of Rights, citing vaccine and mask mandates.

item.title: Town Council votes 6-1 to stop recording closed-session minutes
item.description: Smithfield's Town Council voted 6-1 to halt recording closed-session minutes, ending a practice that had begun roughly seven months earlier.

item.title: Orbit Road closed for construction daily through end of April
item.description: Daytime closures on a 1-mile stretch of Orbit Road near Isle of Wight Academy began March 4 and will continue through the end of April from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.

item.title: Route 17 widening ranked highly in HRTPO 2050 plan
item.description: A plan to widen Route 17 is among the Hampton Roads Transportation Planning Organization's top 2050 priorities, with a $15.9 million first phase already funded.

item.title: Industrial rezoning of Mallory Pointe quarter-acre unrelated to subdivision
item.description: Smithfield's Planning Commission will consider a request on March 10 by the developers of the Mallory Pointe subdivision to rezone a quarter-acre parcel as light industrial, which is unrelated to the 812-home development, according to town officials.

item.title: Letter – Kudos to Short Rows columnist
item.description: Letter: Smithfield resident Joe Puglisi praises John Edwards and The Smithfield Times for a column on Americans’ fundamental rights being under assault.
